Lactobacillus does the work in any vegetable ferment. It is
anaerobic — it wants the oxygen gone, which is why a closed vessel with
the produce fully submerged matters more than any recipe detail.

The sequence is predictable: at the start many microorganisms compete,
then the acid the lactobacilli produce (lactic acid, not acetic) drives
the pH down and they win outright. That acid is the preservative and
the flavour both.

Signs of a healthy ferment: gentle bubbles, milky cloudiness, a sour
smell. Signs of trouble: anything fuzzy on the surface, any smell that
is not sour. When in doubt, the smells are never wrong.
